finding.title: MultiEdit payloads bypass pre:config-protection because run() only inspects top-level file_path or file
finding.detail: hooks/hooks.json:63 registers pre:config-protection with matcher "Write|Edit|MultiEdit", but scripts/hooks/config-protection.js:160 reads only `const filePath = input?.tool_input?.file_path || input?.tool_input?.file || ""` and ignores `input?.tool_input?.edits` (as well as `tool_input.path`). A MultiEdit call with `{ edits: [{ file_path: ".eslintrc.js", old_string: "error", new_string: "off" }] }` or a benign top-level `file_path` paired with a protected path in `edits` returns exitCode 0 and modifies the protected config.
finding.recommendation: Extract all candidate paths from top-level `file_path`/`file`/`path` and every object entry in `tool_input.edits`, and block with exitCode 2 if any target resolves to an existing protected config.

why: Pass 1 appraisal against the lens rubric.

finding.title: Unconditional top-level process.stdin listeners in config-protection.js and post-edit-typecheck.js leak on require()
finding.detail: scripts/hooks/config-protection.js:216-243 and scripts/hooks/post-edit-typecheck.js:20-105 attach `process.stdin.setEncoding("utf8")`, `process.stdin.on("data", ...)`, and `process.stdin.on("end", ...)` at module top level without guarding behind `if (require.main === module)`. When `tests/hooks/hook-input.test.js:10` requires `config-protection.js` with an open stdin descriptor, the process hangs indefinitely after finishing all assertions because the leaked `stdin` data listener keeps the Node.js event loop alive. When required in-process before stdin closes, the top-level `end` listener also races the caller by writing raw stdin to stdout or calling `process.exit(2)`.
finding.recommendation: Wrap the CLI stdin fallback in both `scripts/hooks/config-protection.js` and `scripts/hooks/post-edit-typecheck.js` inside `if (require.main === module)`.

finding.title: post-edit-typecheck.js filters tsc diagnostics with raw line.includes(candidate), causing false positives on root/nested files and missing Windows backslash paths
finding.detail: While `stop-format-typecheck.js:135-143` was updated to parse the leading file path from `tsc --pretty false` diagnostics (`diagnosticMatchesFile`), `post-edit-typecheck.js:84-86` still checks `if (line.includes(candidate)) return true`. When editing root `index.ts` (`relPath = "index.ts"`), `line.includes("index.ts")` matches diagnostics from `src/index.ts(1,14): error TS2322` and `other-index.ts`. Conversely, on Windows where `filePath`, `resolvedPath`, and `relPath` use backslashes (`src\index.ts`) while `tsc` outputs forward slashes (`src/index.ts(1,14)`), `line.includes(candidate)` fails to match any candidate.
finding.recommendation: Replace `line.includes(candidate)` in `post-edit-typecheck.js` with `diagnosticMatchesFile(line, candidates)` that extracts the diagnostic header file path and compares normalized forward-slash paths.
